summary: Normalizes a vector with a length threshold. Computes the squared length v7 over the three spatial components a2[0..2]; if FloatRangeCheck(v7, 1.0) passes the vector is already unit length and all four components of a2 are copied into a1 (or the function returns immediately when a1 == a2). Otherwise, when v7 exceeds 1.1754944e-38, all four components including a2[3] are scaled by v5 = 1.0/sqrt(v7); when v7 is at or below that threshold all four output components are zeroed. Every path writes all four output components, so an external poke to the output does not persist.

local_names.a2: input vector buffer (x,y,z,w), may alias a1
local_names.v7: squared length of the input, computed over spatial components a2[0..2] only
local_names.v5: reciprocal square root 1/sqrt(v7) used as the scaling factor
local_names.v6: computed output component a1[3] on the normalize/zero path
local_names.v4: scratch pointer into the input buffer for the copy path

operations.description: Compute the squared length v7 = a2[0]*a2[0] + a2[1]*a2[1] + a2[2]*a2[2], using only the three spatial components.
Call FloatRangeCheck(v7, 1.0) to test whether the squared length is within the symmetric epsilon band of 1.0, i.e. whether the vector is already unit length.
When FloatRangeCheck returns true the vector is already normalized: copy all four components a2[0..3] into a1, or return immediately when a1 == a2 (in-place call).
When v7 > 1.1754944e-38 compute the scaling factor v5 = 1.0 / sqrt(v7) and scale each input component by it; when v7 <= 1.1754944e-38 the output components are zeroed instead.

Write the four output components: on the already-unit path a straight copy of the input; on the normalization path a1[0..2] = v5 * a2[0..2] and a1[3] = v5 * a2[3]; on the too-small path all four components are zeroed.
Return the output buffer pointer a1.
